cap_rules.hard_cap_note: No default hard cap. Using a tool that an apron forbids hard-caps the team at that apron for the season (e.g. full NT-MLE → hard cap at the 1st apron). Triggers listed follow the forum's rule ('the exception the apron forbids') applied to each restriction — an approximation for the items the forum didn't spell out individually.

sections.title: Salary Cap & Cap Room
items: The salary cap for 2005 is $49,500,000.
Cap room = salary cap − team salary (cap salary, including cap holds and charges). A team with cap room can sign free agents or absorb salary up to the cap.

sections.title: How team salary is calculated
items: Player salaries on the books for the season (active contracts).
Cap holds (count toward the cap only — not the tax or the floor).
Incomplete roster charge (offseason only): one rookie-minimum salary for each player below 12 counted on the books.
Exception holds, while a team is under the cap.
For tax purposes, non-draft free agents earning below the 2-year veteran minimum are counted at the 2-year veteran minimum.
Second-round picks (Rookie Draft rules thread): guaranteed contracts count toward team salary at the index amounts; two-way contracts carry no salary cost.
Note: the forum post lists 8 components; the pasted summary names the ones above. See the forum's 'How Is Team Salary Calculated' post for the complete list.

sections.title: Over vs under the cap
items: By default every team operates as an over-the-cap team (exceptions available: Non-Taxpayer MLE and Bi-Annual Exception, subject to aprons).
Once a team uses its cap room it becomes an under-the-cap team for the season and cannot switch back; only the Room Exception ($2,811,000) remains.

sections.title: Luxury tax
items: Computed on team salary (tax salary) as of the final regular-season game; cap holds and exceptions are excluded.
Tax line: $59,355,126 ($9,855,126 above the cap; measured on team salary, cap holds excluded).
Rates rise in $1,820,000 brackets (see table); every further bracket adds $0.50 per $1.
Repeater: a team that paid tax in at least 3 of the previous 4 seasons pays repeater rates.
About 50% of tax collected is split evenly among non-taxpaying teams; paid at season end.
Example: a non-repeater $5,000,000 over the tax pays $8,855,000.

sections.title: 1st apron ($61,921,126) restrictions
items: No acquiring players via sign-and-trade.
No Bi-Annual Exception.
No full Non-Taxpayer MLE (Taxpayer MLE only).
Cannot sign a waived player whose prior salary exceeded the Non-Taxpayer MLE.
Cannot use trade exceptions from a prior season.
Trades: incoming salary limited to 100% of outgoing (100% salary matching).
Apron restrictions take effect immediately.

sections.title: 2nd apron ($65,723,126) restrictions
items: All 1st-apron restrictions, plus:
No Taxpayer MLE.
No aggregating player salaries in trades.
No cash in trades.
Cannot send players out via sign-and-trade.
The team's 1st-round pick 7 years out is frozen (cannot be traded); it unfreezes if the team is below the 2nd apron in 3 of the next 4 seasons.
If the team is above the 2nd apron in 2 of the next 4 seasons, the frozen pick moves to the end of the 1st round.

sections.title: Hard-cap triggers
items: There is no hard cap by default.
Using an exception or tool that an apron forbids hard-caps the team at that apron for the season — e.g. using the full Non-Taxpayer MLE hard-caps the team at the 1st apron.

sections.title: Salary floor
items: Salary floor = 90% of the cap = $44,550,000.
Cap holds do not count toward the floor.
Any team below the floor when offseason free agency ends will have players auto-signed to reach the floor, and players may be cut as needed to make room.

trade.source: league — official TSFBL trade rules pasted by the user 2026-10-20 (authoritative; manual/trade_rules_full.md). 2nd-apron aggregation / S&T-out / cash limits come from the Aprons Explained text (manual/cap_rules_full.md). Items under 'assumed' are not in league text.
trade.matching_tiers_note: Tier limits increase with the salary cap each season (league note 1) — update these every season.

cap_room_absorption.label: ASSUMED: the league trade text doesn't cover absorbing salary into cap room (it only mentions 'acquired into cap room' for the 40-day aggregation exception). Toggle in Rule settings.

roster_min.label: ASSUMED (standard NBA): 13-man minimum in season (warning only; offseason rosters may be short).

min_salary_max.label: PLACEHOLDER: the league's minimum-salary table isn't available; contracts at or below the NBA 2005-06 10+ year minimum ($1,138,500) are pre-flagged as minimum deals. Toggle per player.

stepien.label: ASSUMED (standard NBA Stepien rule): a team can't be left without a 1st-round pick in consecutive future drafts.

league_cash.label: League cash
league_cash.note: League cash is a separate in-league currency outside the salary cap: it never counts as salary for matching, payroll, tax or aprons. Team balances aren't on the stats site — enter them manually.
league_cash.max_per_trade_note: League rule: Taxpayer MLE rounded DOWN to the nearest $1M (app computes it from exceptions.taxpayer_mle: $1,820,000 → $1,000,000). Exceeding it fails the trade.

trade.second_apron_no_aggregation_source: cap_rules_full.md (Aprons Explained) — not in the trade-rules text

_meta.source: manual — hand-kept league facts (GM list, creation-draft order and results, lottery odds). Not forum posts. Edit by hand; never overwritten by refreshes.
manual — our own concise summaries of league rules the commissioner published/the user pasted (not copies of forum posts). Edit by hand; never overwritten by refreshes.

sections.title: League basics
items: The league mirrors the NBA's current CBA (cap, tax, aprons, exceptions, trade matching) on 2005-06 rosters.
Low-commitment format: inactive GMs and CPU-run teams are handled; regular-season depth charts are fully automated.
Assistant commissioners help with rules questions.

sections.title: Trades (summary)
items: Salary matching applies to every team in the deal, judged on its apron status AFTER the trade.
Below both aprons after the trade: may take back up to 200% + $250K (outgoing ≤ $7.25M), outgoing + $7.5M ($7.25M–$29M), or 125% + $250K (over $29M). Thresholds rise with the cap each season.
Using that table (taking back more than 100%) hard-caps the team at the 1st apron for the season.
Above either apron after the trade: incoming salary may not exceed 100% of outgoing. Above the 2nd apron: no aggregating salaries and no sending league cash.

Minimum-salary players don't count as incoming salary. Sign-and-trade: outgoing = greater of old salary or 50% of new; the receiving team counts the full new salary. Poison pill: receiving team counts the average of the remaining salary plus extension years.

Max 5 players out per team (cash, picks and stashed players don't count). Each team must send a qualifying asset (contracted player, future pick, stashed rights, pick swap, or ≥ $110K league cash; ≥ $1.1M in multi-team deals).

League cash is a separate in-league currency, outside the cap (never counts as salary). Only one team may send it, you can't send more than you have, and teams above the 2nd apron can't send it. Per-trade maximum: Taxpayer MLE rounded down to the nearest $1M ($1M in 2005). First-round picks can never be sold for cash.

Not tradable yet: waiver claims (20 days) and newly signed players (40–60 days). Players acquired by trade can be re-traded at once but not aggregated for 40 days (unless acquired into cap room). You can't reacquire a player you traded or released this league year.
Trades are final, need roster space when posted, and must be in before the scheduled sim. No trades of any kind during the creation draft.

sections.title: Creation draft
items: Order was set by random draw; snake format (order reverses every even round).
Pick clock: 4 hours when on the clock 8 AM–8 PM ET, otherwise 8 hours or until 12 PM ET, whichever is first.
Missing a clock puts you on auto-draft; if you come off it your windows shrink (2 h / 4 h). Three misses = auto-draft for the rest of the draft.
No trades during the creation draft. Drafted players keep their contracts from the start of the 2005-06 NBA season.
No limit on drafted salary, but teams above either apron when the draft ends are bound by the apron rules.

sections.title: Rookie draft
items: Draft threads are for picks only; picks must be submitted on the site (Discord doesn't count) and are final.
Clock 12 PM–8 PM ET: 4 hours in round 1, 2 hours in round 2. An expired clock automates all your remaining picks in that draft.
A pick on the clock can only be traded during its first hour.

sections.title: Second-round picks & contracts
items: Before round 2 a list shows which prospects require a guaranteed deal and which accept a two-way deal (two-way = no salary cost).
Your own 2nd-rounder gets a guaranteed contract unless you ask for two-way. Auto-picks 30–39 get guaranteed deals; auto-picks 40+ come from the two-way pool.
Guaranteed options: 1-yr rookie min, 2-yr rookie min (default), 3-yr min with team option, 4-yr min (starting at the 2-yr min) with team option.
These count against the cap and tax at their listed amounts (not as 2-year-veteran minimums).

sections.title: Draft lottery (3-2-1)
items: 15 teams enter: the 13 non-playoff teams plus both 8-seeds; all 15 picks are drawn.
Balls: the 3 worst records (relegation zone) get 2 each; other non-playoff teams 11th or worse in their conference get 3; 9th–10th get 2; 8-seeds get 1.
Relegation-zone teams can't fall below 12th. No #1 pick in back-to-back years; no top-5 pick three years running (restrictions follow the original owner of the pick).
The first 15 picks of round 2 go in reverse order of round 1. Ties in groupings are settled by a virtual coin flip.

sections.title: Prospect potential
items: A drafted prospect's real potential is set only after the draft, from one of four random methods: historical potential, potential tied to their real draft slot, potential tied to their sim-league draft slot, or fully random.
The scouted potential shown pre-draft is the historical value only. Players in the base file are not affected.

sections.title: Training camp & development
items: Development is run outside the game each offseason and depends on age, potential, playing time, archetype and random variance.
Rookies skip their first camp; G-League assignments give a guaranteed development baseline.

Potential is a guide, not a cap; minor/major/elite breakouts are possible. Skills improve with experience; quickness and jumping peak early, strength into the mid-20s; heavier players decline faster late.

sections.title: Box score claims
items: 1 point each for 50+ pts, 25+ reb, 20+ ast, 10+ stl, 10+ blk, triple-double, 5x5, and Box Score / Player / Rookie / Team of the Sim.
Spend a point as a temporary rating point for the season or a potential point at the next camp, on any player on your roster at the time except the one who earned it.
Playoffs: all regular-season claims except Team of the Sim, counting double. Summer League and Preseason (10 simmed days each) count too; their injuries carry over.
